gaps.category: Reindeer herding co-operatives (paliskunnat) and Sámi/reindeer owners
gaps.first_search: paliskunta poronomistaja ilmoitusvelvollisuus porotilasto poronhoitoilmoitus Paliskuntain yhdistys
gaps.why: Around 50 paliskunta co-operatives and roughly 4,000 owners in Lapland have statutory duties: reindeer register, annual counts, slaughter and compensation reports, predator damage claims. This is a distinctive Finnish small-operator sector and the coverage table never mentions it.

gaps.category: Forest owners and forestry service providers (forest-use declaration, Kemera/state support, felling notices)
gaps.first_search: metsänkäyttöilmoitus pakollinen Metsäkeskus metsänomistaja urakoitsija hakkuu ilmoitus 2026
gaps.why: There are about 600,000 private forest owners and many small contractors. Metsänkäyttöilmoitus to the Finnish Forest Centre is mandatory before felling, and the Forest Act and nature-conservation rules changed. The ledger covers only EUDR for forest owners, not the core forest-use declaration or the support-reporting workflow.

gaps.category: Farm subsidy, CAP and nitrate rules on small family farms (Ruokavirasto)
gaps.first_search: maatila Vipu-palvelu tukihakemus lannoitus muistiinpanot ympäristökorvaus 2026 muutokset pienviljelijä
gaps.why: Farmers face mandatory annual duties: the Vipu support application, parcel and cultivation-plan records, fertiliser-use limits and the new CAP rules from 2025-27. Plant-protection records are touched on, but the wider farm paperwork is not covered, and there are many small family firms.

gaps.category: Small-scale energy producers and heating-system owners (chimney sweeping, fireplace/boiler inspections, solar and heat-pump notifications)
gaps.first_search: nuohous palotarkastus omatoiminen varautuminen pelastuslaki taloyhtiö energiatodistus lämmitysjärjestelmä tarkastus 2026
gaps.why: Pelastuslaki duties fall on households and housing companies: sweeping and fire-safety inspections, and fire-safety self-monitoring for small buildings and associations. The new heating-system rules and the EU building-energy rules (EPBD) add energy-certificate and heating-system inspection duties from 2026-27. None of this is in coverage.

gaps.category: Gambling, lottery and betting-agent premises; alcohol serving and retail licences for small restaurants, cafes and kiosks
gaps.first_search: alkoholilupa anniskelu omavalvonta ravintola Lupa- ja valvontavirasto vuosi-ilmoitus myynti anniskelumaksu
gaps.why: Restaurants and cafes are a very large small-operator group. They must hold alcohol licences from LVV (the former AVI), keep self-monitoring (omavalvonta) records, and report annual alcohol sales volumes. They also have a statutory alcohol-licence fee and Veikkaus or agent-contract rules. Only food-control self-monitoring (Oiva) is covered, not the alcohol regime.

gaps.category: Small exporters and importers: customs, excise and VAT one-stop-shop filings (including the EU customs reform and VAT in the Digital Age)
gaps.first_search: verkkokauppa tulli 150 euron tullivapautuksen poistuminen pienyrittäjä tuonti arvonlisäverokäsittely OSS IOSS 2026
gaps.why: Web shops and small importers face the end of the EU low-value-parcel customs exemption (the 2026 EU duty and handling-fee changes), the excise rules for alcohol and tobacco distance sales, and Tulli authorisations. Intrastat is rejected, but other customs duties on small operators are untouched.

candidates.buyer: Licensed pawn-lending businesses and similar AVI-supervised small obligated entities (currency exchangers, goods dealers). Number of pawnshops not confirmed, likely a few dozen.
candidates.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
candidates.existing: Competitor search 'panttilainaamo ohjelmisto panttilainausjärjestelmä asiakkaan tunteminen rahanpesu' found no pawnshop-specific software. Generic AML screening tools exist, but an in-house pawn system could not be ruled out.
candidates.known_note: K18 rejected scrap and second-hand dealers for lack of a police register. This is a different duty (AML) on a different buyer group (pawnshops).
candidates.name: Pawnshop AML and pawn-ledger compliance kit (customer due diligence, ID retention, source-of-funds, suspicious-transaction reporting)
candidates.trigger: Rahanpesulaki (AML act) supervised by AVI. Pawn lending was raised to the highest risk level in Dec 2023, with intensified supervision in 2024 and 2025. Six pawnshops got sanction fees for failing to verify or prove ID checks, for due diligence and for suspicious-transaction reporting.
candidates.unchecked: Number of licensed pawnshops, whether the AML duty moved to Lupa- ja valvontavirasto in 2026, whether pawn-ledger rules exist beyond AML, and whether the large chains (e.g. Oulun Panttilainakonttori) already have systems. A tiny market.

candidates.buyer: Commercial horse stables and riding schools; estimated thousands of horse keepers, count unverified.
candidates.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
candidates.existing: Competitor search found no Finnish stable software with a legal medication log. Only foreign apps (EquiTrace Pro, EQStable, My Cheval, Hooves). Ratsastajainliitto's tools were not checked.
candidates.name: Stable and riding-school compliance log (animal register changes, medication book, AVI notification)
candidates.trigger: Keeping place and keeping activity registered in Ruokavirasto's EPR before starting, changes within 30 days. Medication log kept 5 years, and horse passports must have medication pages or abattoirs refuse the horse. Commercial keeping of 6 or more adult horses needs a written notice to AVI (animal welfare act). Municipal stable rules vary.
candidates.unchecked: Stable count; whether inspections actually enforce the medication book; Ratsastajainliitto or Hippos tools; and a log is a record, not a periodic filing, so frequency is low.

candidates.buyer: Taxi licence holders (sole traders); the number of licences is in Taksiliitto's 2026 statistics, not read.
candidates.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
candidates.existing: Not checked. Taksiliitto, dispatch and payment apps likely cover part of it.
candidates.name: Taxi licence renewal and professional-competence tracker for sole-trader taxi drivers (licences convert to 10-year terms, first expiries in 2029)
candidates.trigger: Taxi law fixes licences to 10 years and converts open-ended licences, with the first expiring in 2029. Traficom and Verohallinto check tax payments, and licences have been revoked for missing Y-tunnus and missing professional competence.
candidates.unchecked: The 2029 deadline is far away. No competitor search was run (score under 3). Verify the exact rules and whether Traficom already sends reminders.

candidates.buyer: Registered associations, foundations and parties running small fundraisers

candidates.trigger: Rahankeräyslaki: notice to the police for a pienkeräysnumero (19 §), a fundraising account, a tilitys within 2 months of the end, and a notice when funds are used (22 §). The EUR 10,000 and two-per-year limits come from a bill summary and are unconfirmed.
candidates.unchecked: Each association files only occasionally, so low frequency and low willingness to pay.

candidates.name: Lift-inspection and maintenance tracker for small lift owners
candidates.trigger: Hissiturvallisuuslaki 1134/2016: inspection every 2 years, maintenance programme, defects fixed promptly, documents available to inspectors.

candidates.buyer: Farmers and contractors who are professional pesticide users
candidates.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
candidates.existing: Farm-management software is likely to cover it, unchecked.

candidates.unchecked: No competitor check, the record is kept on the farm rather than filed, and it was not shown that farm software lacks it.

candidates.trigger: Animal-keeper and keeping-place registration with Ruokavirasto before starting, and changes within 30 days. A primary-production notice to municipal food control for honey.
candidates.unchecked: Minimal duties and a free state service.

candidates.existing: Not checked.

candidates.trigger: From work performed after 1 Jan 2026 the client must file a separate Verohallinto notice, and the 2026 income-register spec adds two income-earner types.
candidates.unchecked: Very narrow buyer group, and these firms are mid-size.

candidates.buyer: Hunting clubs and permit holders

candidates.evidence: Riistakeskus guidance riista.fi/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/alueen-pyyntiluvan-ja-metsastyksenjohtajien-paivittaminen-ryhmaan-2024-2025.pdf (found in search, not opened); search summary says Oma riista is the authorities' online service for licences and harvest reports.

candidates.buyer: Scrap dealers
candidates.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
candidates.evidence: https://yle.fi/a/74-20119188 ; https://yle.fi/a/74-20146511 (Yle says law does not allow a cash ban)
candidates.existing: Suomen romukauppiaiden liitto theft-report form and its own system.
candidates.known_note: Same buyer and duty as K18. I found no new rule, so no revive.
candidates.name: Scrap-dealer theft-alert and seller-ID system
candidates.trigger: Dealers check seller identity and metal origin by practice, with no statutory register found.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Verohallinto's free Palkka.fi service calculates and pays wages and files the income-register notice automatically for households (vero.fi/tulorekisteri/yksityishenkilöt/kotitalous-työnantajana). TyEL pension insurance, accident insurance and a sickness-insurance contribution above EUR 1,500/year (2024 figures) are the other duties. A free state tool already covers the core job. No gap found.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K18. Yle (yle.fi/a/74-20146511, yle.fi/a/74-20119188) says current law does not allow a cash ban. Dealers use the Suomen romukauppiaiden liitto theft-report form and an internal system, and I found no statutory police register or record-keeping duty. No revive evidence.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: AVI (Southern Finland) raised pawnshops to the highest AML risk level in Dec 2023, inspected 8 in 2024 and continues in 2025. Six pawnshops got sanction fees for missing ID verification, due diligence and suspicious-transaction reporting (sttinfo.fi release; Kaleva reports a EUR 14,000 fee on Oulun Panttilainakonttori Oy). Candidate C1. No second-hand dealer register found, consistent with K18.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No gold-buyer register or notification duty found in two searches. Pawnshops (C1) are the visible gold buyers. AVI's 2024 AML inspections also covered a goods dealer and a currency exchanger. Dealer-level duty unverified.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Passenger cars and vans can only be deregistered at an official take-back point of Suomen Autokierrätys Oy, which issues the destruction certificate and files the deregistration (Traficom/suomi.fi). The workflow is closed and centralised. A 2026-2027 scrappage bonus (EUR 2,000-2,500, vehicles from 2015 or earlier, valtioneuvosto.fi) is paid by Traficom to car buyers, not dismantlers. Nothing sellable found.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animal transporter licences and a transporter register exist, with AVI issuing competence certificates. I found no trader-specific reporting that is a gap. Keepers, including horse stables and riding schools, must register the keeping place and the keeping activity in Ruokavirasto's EPR (epr.ruokavirasto.fi) and report changes within 30 days. Commercial stables with 6 or more adult horses also notify AVI under the animal welfare act, and a medication log is kept 5 years. Candidate C2.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Ruokavirasto's guide to starting a meat plant has a self-monitoring plan chapter (osa 5 omavalvonta). A 2016 study says small slaughterhouses find self-monitoring heavy. It is a one-off plan plus ongoing records, with no periodic filing. Municipal food control moves to Ruokavirasto in the 2026 reform (municipal documents, unconfirmed). Nothing concrete.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Keepers register with Ruokavirasto's animal register before keeping bees and report changes within 30 days. Honey production under 2,500 kg/year gets primary-production relief and a notification to municipal food control. Low frequency and few duties. Weak candidate C7.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K10. Searches returned the vet register and EU Regulation 2019/6 only, with no Finnish medicine-sales reporting rule found.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: No driller licensing register or general household-well notification found. Helsinki guidance says a shared or private well supplying at least 50 people or 10 m3/day must be notified, which falls under K04 water cooperatives. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: The waste authority keeps a register of sludge-tank emptyings, and property owners are told to use hauliers listed in the jätehuoltorekisteri. Emptying intervals are set by each municipality (e.g. Kaavi: septic tank yearly, holding tank at least every 5 years). The 2019 renovation deadline has passed and no new one is planned. Haulers fall under K02, and the owner side is a fragmented, low-pain duty. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Under the lift safety act (1134/2016) the holder must arrange inspections every 2 years and keep a maintenance programme (Kiwa, Isännöintiliitto). Buyers are housing companies and property managers, which sits close to K14 (rejected, dominated by property-management suites). Candidate C5 is weak. Pressure equipment not checked in detail.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04. A water utility without its own intake or treatment files a notification, and one with its own intake or treatment needs approval (hel.fi water-supply notifications page).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: All professional users, and at least one seller per business, need the plant-protection certificate (Act 1563/2011). Users keep records of product, area, crop and amount applied. ELY centres inspect under Ruokavirasto direction, and failure to produce the usage records is a recorded violation (Ruokavirasto 2019 control report). Farm software competition not checked. Weak candidate C6.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No agency registration regime found. New from 1 Jan 2026: a client using a foreign temporary worker on a Finnish vessel or aircraft must file a separate Verohallinto notice (form 6146), and the 2026 income-register spec adds two income-earner types. Very narrow buyer group (shipping clients). Weak candidate C8.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Parish cemeteries run under the Funeral Act (457/2003) and church rules. A 2024 planning document lists funeral permit, supervision and funding tasks for the new Lupa- ja valvontavirasto (which began operating 1 Jan 2026). I found no register or periodic duty for private funeral firms. Unverified whether a private-firm duty exists.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Small fundraising by registered associations needs a police notification, a fundraising account, a pienkeräystilitys within 2 months of the end, and a notice when the money is spent (Rahankeräyslaki 19 and 22 §). It is occasional per association, so candidate C4 is weak. The PRH beneficial-owner duty found covers companies and cooperatives, and association coverage is unverified. Halal and kosher supervision: not searched.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi: licences are now fixed 10-year, and existing open-ended licences convert and start expiring in 2029. Traficom and Verohallinto checked over 1,500 licence holders' payments, and over 500 licences were revoked for no Y-tunnus (moottori.fi, 2022). Taksiliitto publishes statistics and Traficom issues 2026 orders on taxi training and exams. Candidate C3 is weak and unverified. Small trucking and minibus: not searched separately.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Market trade is governed by each municipality's torisäännöt and holders handle their own permits and taxes. Mobile food sellers must notify food control 4 working days ahead of each municipality (Hamina 2015 guide, possibly outdated). Money changers: AVI inspected one in 2024 under the AML act. The old virtual-currency register was replaced by MiCA authorisation, and its transition ended 30 June 2026 (Finanssivalvonta release 13/2026). Nothing sellable beyond the AML point under C1.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Tattoo: Valvira guideline TO 7.1 (2014) covers skin-piercing premises under the health protection act, but I could not confirm the notification procedure or any periodic report. Driving schools: need a Traficom autokoululupa with named teaching staff (Minilex), and no ongoing report was found. Nurseries and childminders: K12 and K06. Hunting: harvest reports within 7 days and hunt leaders go through the state Oma riista portal, so it is not a gap. Small food producers: only meat plants checked (category 7).

candidates.buyer: About 50,000 volunteer-run tiekunnat (chairman or treasurer), plus the road-manager firms that serve them
candidates.category: 31. Private road associations (tiekunnat)
candidates.evidence: https://valtioneuvosto.fi/-/1410829/hallitus-esittaa-muutoksia-yksityistielakiin (WebFetch blocked with 403, so details come from the search summary); https://www.edilex.fi/he/20260125; https://www.kaleva.fi/tiekunnista-tekoalyajan-palvelualustoja/13615221 (about 50,000 tiekunnat); https://lutpub.lut.fi/handle/10024/164236 (LUT thesis on automatic tiekunta bookkeeping). Some firms sell outsourced services (bookkeeping, meeting notices, road-fee billing, shareholder registers).
candidates.existing: Outsourced road-manager firms (TIKO-tieisännöitsijä, Marin kirjanpito ja tieisännöintipalvelut) and an academic prototype. I found no dominant tiekunta software. The Kaleva piece may describe a platform, but that is unverified.
candidates.known_note: Same board-binder concept as K04, but a different buyer group (road associations rather than water co-ops) and a different duty.
candidates.name: Tiekunta (private road association) administration and shareholder-register platform
candidates.trigger: Government proposal to amend the Private Roads Act (yksityistielaki) submitted 2.7.2026, effective 1.1.2027: duty to keep a shareholder register, easier member access to documents, road-fee appeals, simpler decision-making. Existing duties: annual budget meeting, road units, fee billing.
candidates.unchecked: The reform's final wording and passage in Parliament; whether the HE number is 125/2026 as Edilex implies; how many tiekunnat actually keep books or hold meetings; willingness to pay; the Kaleva platform; Maanmittauslaitos tools and pricing of the outsourced firms.

candidates.unchecked: Final decree text and entry into force; number of firms and equipment owners; whether generic service-management or cooling-vendor software already has an F-gas log; whether reporting to an authority is required beyond keeping the log.

result.competitor: Tievahti (tievahti.fi, app.tievahti.fi) is a web service built for tiekunnat, and it is free "now and in the future". It covers roads and properties, shareholders, road units, linking a bank account, billing road fees, bookkeeping, meeting notices, running meetings, and archiving documents. It has a municipal portal (kunta.tievahti.fi), municipalities use it for private-road grant applications, and it works with Maanmittauslaitos, Metsäkeskus and Elinvoimakeskus. It makes money from paid road-manager (tieisännöinti) and bearing-capacity measurement services. Other options: TIKO-certified road-manager firms such as Marin kirjanpito ja tieisännöintipalvelut handle shareholder lists, unit calculations and fee billing. Municipalities also run their own registers, such as Tiekuntarekisteri.fi hosted by Matriset Oy and Äänekoski's Wintie.
result.duty: Real, but the new part is not yet law. The government bill amending the Private Roads Act (yksityistielaki 560/2018), HE 125/2026, went to Parliament on 2.7.2026 with a planned start date of 1.1.2027. It would make the tiekunta's governing body (toimielin) keep a shareholder register (osakasluettelo) and give shareholders easier access to documents. It also changes road-fee appeals and governance. I did not check whether Parliament has passed it. Duties already in force: keep the association's details current in the Maanmittauslaitos private road register, hold the annual meeting, keep road-unit records and bill road fees. In practice no penalty applies. The sanction is that disputes go to Maanmittauslaitos road proceedings or court, and municipal or state grants depend on proper records.
result.market: About 50,000 tiekunnat, a figure taken from a Kaleva reader's opinion piece and not checked against the Maanmittauslaitos register. Most are tiny, volunteer-run and spend very little.
result.reason: The duty is real, and the 2027 bill would add a formal shareholder-register duty. But Tievahti already does the core job for free: it handles shareholders, road units, road-fee billing, bookkeeping, meetings and document archiving. Municipalities also use it for grant applications. Road-manager firms cover the outsourced, done-for-you end of the market. The buyers are volunteer boards that spend little, and a free, government-linked incumbent is already in place, so there is almost no room for a paid tool from a solo founder. The Kaleva article is an opinion piece about the STEK project, not a product. The claim's "no dominant tiekunta software" is wrong.

The AML duty is real and in force: the Rahanpesulaki applies to pawn lenders, and the regional agency (AVI) ran intensified supervision after rating pawn lending highest risk in Dec 2023. Six pawnshops got sanction fees, including 14,000 EUR for Oulun Panttilainakonttori. Supervision has since moved to Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, which started 1.1.2026. Searches found no Finnish pawnshop AML or ledger software, only foreign pawn systems. The market is tiny: AVI did 8 pawnshop inspections in 2024, and the real count is probably a few dozen. Willingness to pay is limited, and the larger chains likely have in-house systems. Not checked: the official number of licensed pawnshops, and any pawn-ledger rules beyond AML. The score stays low because of the market size.

Duty is real: horse keeping places must be registered, and ammattimainen or large-scale keeping needs a written notice. The threshold is unclear. The claim says 6 adult horses to AVI. Oulu material citing the horse welfare decree 321/2025 says 7 to Ruokavirasto, and I could not check the law text. I found no Finnish stable software with a legal medication log, only foreign tools (Equine Medirecord, Die Pferde App). Ratsastajainliitto and Hippos tools were not checked. Market is roughly 16,000 stables and 67,300 horses (Hevosala lukuina 2025), but most are private. The duty is event-driven record keeping, not a periodic filing. Frequency is low, enforcement is weak and willingness to pay is small, so the score is low.

Duty partly real: Minilex says open-ended ELY taxi licences become fixed-term, new/renewed licences last 10 years, first expiries 2029, and Traficom says it will remind holders before expiry. That reminder, plus Traficom's online filing, undercuts a tracker. Traficom's page also lists 2026 changes: 21h training, a medical report, and 7h refresher training for driver-licence renewal between 1 Nov 2026 and 31 Aug 2034. Fixed expiry dates are a one-off per licence and 2029 is far off. I found no competing software, but I did not read the Taksiliitto licence count or the primary law text. Buyers are sole traders, a fragmented market with low willingness to pay, and Traficom's own reminders cover the core job.

Duty is real. The Hissiturvallisuuslaki 1134/2016 requires the holder to keep a maintenance programme, fix defects promptly, and have periodic inspections every 2 years by Tukes-approved bodies. Documents must be available to maintainers and inspectors. Penalty and in-force status were not checked directly. No dedicated lift-tracker software for housing companies turned up. Maintenance firms (KONE sensor monitoring) and inspection bodies (Kiwa) cover the core job. Property managers handle it as part of management suites, which is why K14 was rejected. Buyers are fragmented, the inspection is only every 2 years, and the inspectors already send reminders. Willingness to pay is low and the buyer is the same as K14's. Market size was not quantified. Score stays low.

result.duty: Registration of social and health service providers and service units in Soteri before operating (law in force since 2024); LVV from 2026; updates when details change; fees apply.
result.reason: The duty is real. Since 2024, private social and health providers must register in Valvira's Soteri register. Registration is a precondition for operating. From 1.1.2026 the new Lupa- ja valvontavirasto took over, and the government set new 2026 registration fees. But this is mostly a one-off registration plus occasional updates, not a recurring workflow. The state e-service Soteri is the free official channel, and it lets providers update some details without authority processing. A software layer has little to do: pain was queue delays, not paperwork. Willingness to pay is low, and the claim is a known idea (K03). I did not verify the 2028 transition or the exact fee amounts. I did not search for commercial competitors, and I did not look up a register count of providers.

Duty is not yet law. HE 83/2026 vp (submitted 30.4.2026) would add a Building Act duty to keep a record of short-term rental days and show it to building control on request. The 90/180-day limits apply only in detailed-plan areas to non-primary dwellings, and the sections would start from 1.1.2027. I found no evidence of passage as of 9.10.2026, only a committee opinion (TaVL 20/2026). Finland has no registration duty. Yle (14.7.2025) says TEM has no register measures pending, so the EU 2024/1028 number system is unconfirmed here. No penalty or fine is stated in what I saw. No Finnish competitor found, but the search was thin. The duty is only record-keeping on request, with weak enforcement, and the host count is unknown. Platforms and generic PMS/calendar tools could cover it. Low pain, low willingness to pay.
